statement: Given a normalized external manifest, one installable artifact owner resolves remote OCI descriptor bytes or an OCI image-layout descriptor through the same verification path, recomputes the declared sha256 digest, verifies the declared container or WASM payload media type, and enforces an explicit detached-signature policy with typed fail-closed outcomes, without persisting catalog state or activating a runtime.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The owner is src/service/installable-service-artifact-resolver.js, exported through src/service/index.js and proved by test/service/installable-service-artifact-resolver.test.js via scripts/checks/run-installable-service-artifact-owner-scenarios.js; architecture/lagrange-service-registry.md may document the executable boundary. No other production owner is in scope.

Remote OCI providers and local OCI image layouts may differ only in descriptor acquisition. Both must feed the same bounded descriptor digest, OCI-manifest shape, payload-media, and signature-policy verification path.

Signature handling has no implicit default: required, verify_if_present, and disabled are explicit modes. Required and present signatures use detached Ed25519 verification over the canonical sha256 digest against configured trusted public keys; missing, malformed, invalid, or untrusted required evidence fails closed.

The scenario must reject unsupported sources, provider failures, invalid OCI layout/index/manifest shapes, absent descriptors, oversized descriptors, digest and descriptor-size mismatches, container/WASM media mismatches, and every signature-policy failure while accepting both runtime media types through remote and local sources.

This Quest does not implement registry authentication or wire protocol, build a local layout, persist packages or installations, submit lifecycle mutations, pull container layers into an engine, load WASM bytes, or activate runtimes.

Independent verification must show the scenario turns red when digest comparison, runtime/media pairing, or required-signature enforcement is bypassed, and must verify exact-patch plus aggregate fingerprints before checkpoint and handoff.
